description: Committed candidate sets for the restoration constraint sweep. Each case is one out-of-vocabulary query token with the near candidates the typo step would see, plus the selection every swept setting must make. The three constants are separable here: a case is written so that exactly one of them changes its outcome.

cases.why: 'sut' was typed for 'суть'; only 'суть' romanizes back to it. A budget of 1 also admits 'суд', and the two then tie on every signal, so the short-token refusal fires and the CORRECT restoration is lost as well.

'rishennya' romanizes back to 'рішення' exactly. A budget of 1 also admits 'рішенню', which is a different case of the same noun and sorts first, so the relaxed budget rewrites the user's inflection on a token long enough that no tie refusal protects it.
Deleting a character from a four-character token yields a different short word, not a repair. Only a cutoff of 3 stops treating 'хіта' as short and lets the deletion through.
The mirror image: raising the cutoff to 5 starts refusing length changes on five-character tokens, where a dropped letter is still a plausible typo.
'наказ' is the known word form; 'накат' is what a query about waves co-occurs with. The two signals disagree, so the tie-break order alone decides which corpus surface the query is rewritten to.
